findings.title: Existing recovery intent makes trusted unknown-submission recovery roll back
findings.trigger: A submission_unknown job still has its original outbox intent after a crash or expired acknowledgement. resolveSubmissionUnknown receives a valid complete ProviderSubmissionAck after the job lease expires.
findings.actual_behavior: ensureOutbox returns false when an intent already exists (sqlite.ts:189-199), which is treated as an exception. The surrounding transaction rolls back the new receipt, provider reference and running state.
findings.expected_behavior: Persist the trusted reference and receipt while preserving an existing intent and claim; ensureOutbox must create only if missing. Existing recovery intent is not a failure.
reproduction_steps: Enqueue and claim an eligible job, transition submitting then submission_unknown without finishOutbox (simulate crash after transition).
Advance store time beyond job and outbox lease expiration.
Call resolveSubmissionUnknown with the exact job full honored-input receipt and known provider reference.
Observe exception A reconciliation outbox intent already exists and unchanged submission_unknown job with no receipt/reference committed.
Regression should show running state, persisted receipt, unchanged existing intent identity/claim and resumed polling with zero submit calls.
findings.validation: Static deterministic transaction-path audit; reviewer did not execute this regression.

findings.title: Stop provider work when heartbeat or job ownership is lost
findings.trigger: An in-flight poll outlives its lease, heartbeat returns false, and another worker claims the job.
findings.actual_behavior: The heartbeat result is discarded; poll loop checks only cancel_requested status (lines 84-90), never leaseToken or deadline. Old worker can keep polling indefinitely, download/store results, and call provider.cancel if the new owner sees cancellation. Database CAS blocks old commits but does not stop stale provider/filesystem work.
findings.expected_behavior: Record heartbeat failure and terminate owned processing. Recheck live token/status before subsequent provider poll/cancel/download work, so only current job owner performs side effects.
reproduction_steps: Seed running job with provider reference and outbox, then start worker A with deferred/running provider poll.
Expire its injected clock beyond lease deadline before heartbeat; let worker B claim same job.
Release A poll as running and its wait; observe A issues another poll despite changed job leaseToken.
Request cancellation; observe stale A may call provider.cancel for a job owned by B.
Regression should assert no further A poll/cancel/download after ownership loss and unchanged B-owned job.
findings.validation: Static state-machine audit; reviewer did not execute fault-injection regression.
